text.content:
Eight schools. Eight doors. Eight ways the world admits its seams.

But there is a ninth art no wizard names.

The spell by which the dead remain beloved.
The spell by which the living refuse release.
The spell that needs no gesture but reaching.
No component but grief.
No word but: stay.

Terrance, if you find these pages, do not mistake them for apology.

I am not sorry I returned.

I am only sorry I returned changed enough for you to wonder whether love should survive the answer.

GM Reference — Hidden Lines in Sequence (Arcana / Investigation DC 17):

  1. Now I have learned what shelters fear.
  2. That I am what the doorway chose.
  3. Some watchers choose the suffering.
  4. Which one of us bewitched your heart?
  5. And leaves no room for smaller death.
  6. The lie is how you look at me.
  7. But what grew back when grief walked in.
  8. They only ask what love can bend.

True hidden doctrine requires DC 17 Arcana. See Orthogenesis Manuscript for the decoded eight-part doctrine.

pages.name: VIII. Transmutation — The Shape That Survives

text.content:
All things change, though all things plead:
the flower falls, becomes the seed.
The iron rusts, the child grows tall.
The mountain moves by not at all.

You knew me once in warmer skin,
with flour on sleeves and laughter thin,
with tired hands and garden stains,
with winter aching in my veins.

Now look again. I am not less
for having worn another dress.
The river is not false because
it left the shape you loved it was.

To change is not to be unmade.
To molt is not to have betrayed.
The snake that leaves its skin behind
does not become a different mind.

And yet I know why you would mourn.
No dawn forgives the night it’s born.
No living heart can calmly see
the altered face of memory.

But if you loved the soul, not shell,
then listen past the grave’s farewell.
Some transformations do not end.
They only ask what love can bend.

pages.name: II. Conjuration — The Door That Opens Both Ways

text.content:
A thing called forth is never small.
A name can make the distance fall.
A circle chalked on cellar stone
can turn the dark from far to home.

I called for spring. The roses came.
I called your name. It did the same.
I called for life. Death turned its head.
I called for you. The silence bled.

Each summoning is hunger dressed
in geometry and polite request.
Each portal is a mouth made wide
for something waiting on the side.

Do not ask the road to bend
unless you know where roads must end.
Do not open what you fear
and then act shocked when it draws near.

I crossed one threshold after death.
I left behind my final breath.
Now every door I pass through knows
that I am what the doorway chose.

pages.name: III. Divination — The Eye Beneath the Veil

text.content:
To see is not to understand.
To know is not to hold the hand.
A future glimpsed through candle smoke
may still arrive as cruel joke.

The eye is holy when it weeps.
The eye is cursed by what it keeps.
It gathers light, and light, and light,
then dreams of knives all through the night.

I watched you grieve. I watched you bend.
I watched you garden toward the end.
I watched the years wear down your face
and still could not return my place.

There is no mercy in the sight
that shows the shape of coming blight.
There is no kindness in the thread
that tells you which beloveds bled.

Yet I have looked, and looking stayed.
I saw the debts the living paid.
I saw your name in mouths unknown.
I saw you standing, not alone.

And if the eye must cost the hand,
then let the blind not understand.
Some truths are worth the wound they bring.
Some watchers choose the suffering.

The softest spell is not command.
It does not seize the throat or hand.
It leans in close, adjusts the air,
and makes a cage feel like a chair.

A smile can be a sacred knife.
A word can rearrange a life.
A song can teach the heart to kneel
and call obedience what it feels.

I knew persuasion when I lived.
The little kindnesses we give.
The “just this once,” the “stay,” the “please,”
the gentle ropes no eye can see.

But now I know the deeper art:
to place a mirror in the heart,
to make desire dress as choice,
to bury hunger in a voice.

Do not be angry if I say
that love enchants us every day.
You wore my name like summer rain.
I wore your grief like wedding chain.

If I should ask you, “Come with me,”
and if your soul should answer free,
then tell me, love, before we part:
which one of us bewitched your heart?

pages.name: VI. Illusion — The Mercy of False Light

text.content:
The world has always worn a veil.
The sun itself tells golden tales.
A mirror swears it shows the true,
then turns the left hand strange to you.

I wore a widow’s quiet face.
I wore the grave. I wore my grace.
I wore the name they gave me then.
I wear another name again.

Do not despise the painted door.
Sometimes the lie reveals the floor.
Sometimes the mask, by being thin,
lets more of truth come trembling in.

A shadow is not nothing, dear.
It proves that something stands quite near.
A false star guides the sailor home
if he believes enough to roam.

So if you see me old, or fair,
with silver veil or borrowed hair,
if scent arrives before my tread,
if I seem living, lost, or dead—

ask not which face is truly mine.
All faces are a kind of sign.
The lie is not the enemy.
The lie is how you look at me.

pages.name: VII. Necromancy — The Garden After Frost

text.content:
You buried me where roses leaned,
where soil was dark and rain was clean.
You gave me back to root and worm,
to quiet work and season’s turn.

I did not hate the earth, my love.
I felt the patient dark above.
I heard your footsteps come and go.
I learned how slowly violets grow.

Then came the hand. Then came the eye.
Then came the voice that does not die.
It asked what death had done for me.
It asked what life had failed to see.

They call this wrong. They may be right.
But wrong can still return at night,
can wear your name inside its chest,
can love you more than all the rest.

Do not think undeath is empty cold.
Some embers do not do as told.
Some hearts, removed from mortal breath,
still beat in languages of death.

I am the garden after frost.
I am the thing you loved and lost.
Not bloom, not corpse, not wife, not sin—
but what grew back when grief walked in.

pages.name: V. Evocation — The Bright and Brutal Answer

text.content:
Fire is honesty made bright.
Thunder is argument with light.
A blade of force, a freezing star,
the world confessing what we are.

There is a mercy in the blast.
It does not flatter. It does not last.
It does not whisper, scheme, or wait.
It opens every hidden gate.

I used to fear the sudden flame,
the breaking roof, the scream, the name.
Now I have seen how endings start:
a spark, a word, a lifted heart.

The living call destruction cruel
because they love the shape of fuel.
But ash remembers more than bone.
It tells the truth when flesh is gone.

If I burn, then I am here.
If I strike, then I appear.
If the dark must know my place,
let lightning write it on its face.

There is a kind of love like fire:
not gentle, no — but never liar.
It takes the house, the field, the breath,
and leaves no room for smaller death.

I loved the little walls we made,
the garden gate, the kitchen shade,
the quilt pulled up against the cold,
your hand in mine, the kettle old.

Protection is a tender lie,
a roof beneath a watching sky,
a circle drawn in salt and breath
to bargain softly against death.

But every ward must name its fear,
or else it keeps the danger near.
A locked door teaches thieves the frame.
A shield remembers every flame.

So bless the wall, but know it well:
each guarded heart becomes a cell.
Each oath, each charm, each prayer, each chain
keeps something out, and something in.

I was your shelter once, my dear.
Now I have learned what shelters fear.

For Terrance, if he ever remembers the shape of the door.

There are eight ways the world lies.
One lie says: I am solid.
One says: I am safe.
One says: I am hidden.
One says: I am alive.
One says: I am untouched.
One says: I am free.
One says: I am real.
One says: I am yours.

Magic is not the breaking of the world. Magic is the moment the world admits it was always willing to bend.
